item.title: Fermin Lopez talks Lamine Yamal, Dani Olmo competition, losses to PSG and Real Madrid: ‘He’s the best’
item.description: Fermin Lopez talks Lamine Yamal, Dani Olmo competition, losses to PSG and Real Madrid: ‘He’s the best’ In an interview with Mundo Deportivo , Barcelona midfielder Fermin Lopez hailed teammate Lamine Yamal as the best player in the world. The 23-year-old La Masia graduate, who recently made his 150th appearance for Barcelona in the win against Aston Villa, also discussed the competition for places in the team, particularly with Dani Olmo, while also opening up about the team’s recent form. On partnership with Lamine Yamal and Olmo It was pointed out to Fermin during the interview that Lamine, in a recent media appearance, had revealed that he enjoyed playing with the 23-year-old star due to the connection they share on the pitch. Elaborating on the said connection, Fermin explained: “It means a lot because for me he’s the best, and the fact that he feels comfortable with me as a player, and that we have that rapport and connection, is important to me and to the team. “I’ve known Lamine since we were kids, and when you have a friend off the field, you have that rapport too, and it’s even easier on the field. You know each other perfectly, and I think he and I know each other one hundred percent. “That’s what we try to do on the field, and I’m very happy to play with him because, honestly, he’s the best.” Lamine and Fermin share an excellent partnership. (Photo by Burak Kara/Getty Images) Fermin has had to share time with Olmo in the attacking midfield position under Hansi Flick, and the academy graduate relishes the challenge and competition. “It’s a really good competition because he’s a very good player, and in the end, we both try to make the most of our opportunities and do what’s best for ourselves. But we get along really well off the field; it’s a very healthy competition,” he said. “Ultimately, we’re teammates, and we get along well with each other, even when the other isn’t playing. The competition makes us better every day, and I think that’s important.” On team’s form and recent losses After enjoying a scintillating start to the season, winning 11 games in 11, Barcelona fell to back-to-back defeats against PSG and Real Madrid. Since then, the Catalans have managed to bounce back with victories over Alaves and Aston Villa. But ahead of tomorrow’s clash against Atletico Madrid there remain some lingering doubts about the team’s ability and performances against the big teams. Talking about what happened to the team leading to the Clasico defeat, Fermin explained: “I think what happened to us is that we weren’t sharp. We weren’t playing the way we had been, and that’s why people probably thought we were going to win by a landslide. Obviously, we didn’t, because it’s Real Madrid and they can beat you in any match. “We weren’t good, and everything went perfectly for them. Their first goal is what it is, and you’re already playing against the current in a match where you’re not comfortable with the ball, and everything becomes more difficult.”

item.title: My dream is to win Ballon d'Or - Gabriel
item.description: Gabriel played against Atletico Madrid on Manchester United's pre-season tour [Getty Images] Manchester United forward JJ Gabriel says his "dream is to win the Ballon d'Or", as he closes in on a move to Real Madrid. The 16-year-old is still registered at United but has been training on his own in Spain after walking out on the club and relocating with his family. He has subsequently reached a verbal agreement to join Real Madrid but no deal has been signed as yet. On Friday, following one of his sessions, the teenager was approached by Spanish news outlet Marca who presented him with a copy of their newspaper, which featured a front-page story about his expected move to Los Blancos. The newspaper reported he told them in English: "My dream is to win a Ballon d'Or." United would be due compensation should Gabriel leave, although the figure will be lower if he signs for a club outside the Premier League. Though no club-to-club talks have been held, sources have told BBC Sport that Real have verbally agreed a deal with Gabriel and his representatives. Despite United having Gabriel's registration domestically, it is not thought it could prevent the youngster joining a club overseas as he now has a European Union passport through his mother, who has Cypriot origin. While Real and United are both in the Uefa Youth League this season, competition rules prevent players from appearing for more than one club in a single season and Gabriel scored a hat-trick in his final appearance for United against Sabah in September. He was named the Premier League's Under-18 player of the season last term, despite being only 14 when the season began. item.title: “I Can’t Trade Aaron Judge” – Yankees Sportscaster Bluntly Rejects Hypothetical Deal That Would Bring Pete Crow-Armstrong & Tarik Skubal To NY
item.description: Aaron Judge - New York Yankees | © Imagn New York Yankees sportscaster Michael Kay faced a wild trade proposal involving captain Aaron Judge and Chicago Cubs NL MVP favorite Pete Crow-Armstrong. On Thursday’s Michael Kay Show, a caller named Tony from Dobbs Ferry suggested a hypothetical trade sending Judge to the Cubs for PCA, shortstop Nico Hoerner, and Japanese ace Shota Imanaga. Kay respectfully declined the hypothetical trade for obvious reasons. “First of all, I don’t think that the Cubs would offer that for Judge,” Kay said. “I mean, you have the guy who’s going to win the National League MVP. Nico Hoerner is a beast, and Imanaga is a pretty good pitcher. So I don’t think that they would offer that… I would have to say I would have to respectfully decline. I cannot trade the face of my franchise. I can’t, even if the deal makes total sense. I absolutely cannot do it… Sometimes things are bigger than, you know, what makes sense on a chart. Things are bigger. I can’t trade Aaron Judge. I can’t have my fan base revolt.” The caller added that the trade is meant to free up payroll tied to Judge’s nine-year, $360 million contract , allowing the Yankees to go after Tarik Skubal in free agency. However, Kay still declined. “But I don’t need starting pitching,” Kay continued. “Skubal is terrific. He’s a great pitcher who’s also had three elbow surgeries. He’s terrific, two Cy Young Awards, I love him, but I don’t need him. That’s not what the Yankees need. It should be good enough to have Cam Schlittler up top, and Cole and Fried and Rodón. They don’t need another starting pitcher.” Kay added that trading Judge out of New York wouldn’t earn the franchise any favor with fans. Moreover, even from Chicago’s side, the deal makes “no sense” because they’ll be trading for a soon-to-be 35-year-old outfielder. Yankees Get Good News on Aaron Judge’s Rehab Aaron Judge ended up missing the entire postseason after struggling with a calf strain late in the regular season. The Yankees won their Wild Card series against the Boston Red Sox, but were swept by the Tampa Bay Rays in the ALDS. There was a chance Judge could feature in the ALCS in limited capacity had the Yankees gone through. In the latest Yankees’ injury report , the club expects the captain to be ready for 2027 Spring Training. The report said the Yankees outfielder has a moderate-grade strain of the soleus muscle in his right calf. Moreover, he is scheduled to visit Dr. Gregory Pearl for his rib injury he sustained early in the season. This is an encouraging update for the Yankees, who were unsure how to use Judge in the postseason despite the injury. While that never came to pass, opinions were divided on whether the Yankees would play Judge despite the injury , given the severity of his calf strain. According to MARCA , the Portuguese manager is not only looking at traditional squad rotation, but is also incorporating individual rest periods, additional days off and measures designed to help players recover away from football. Simply put, Mourinho’s desire is to prevent fatigue and reduce injury risks during a demanding campaign. With Real Madrid competing across multiple competitions, managing the physical condition of key players has become an important part of his planning, which is quite crucial given Real Madrid’s history with injuries . Mourinho takes inspiration from Luis Enrique’s PSG approach The outlet mentions that Luis Enrique has regularly managed the workload of his regular starting players at PSG, giving them opportunities to rest during the first half of the campaign rather than waiting until fatigue becomes a problem. Mourinho is now looking to introduce a similar philosophy at Real Madrid, although the approach will be adapted to the demands of Spanish football. Notably, Arda Guler and Aurelien Tchouameni were among the first players to benefit from the strategy during the match against AEK. Mourinho is planning to copy Luis Enrique’s strategy. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) In fact, the Portuguese manager intends to extend the approach to other members of his squad as the season progresses. Simply put, the plan involves not just substituting players or changing the starting XI. Rather, selected footballers will receive additional time away from training and matches to recover mentally and physically. Real Madrid introduce individual workload management Mourinho is working alongside different departments at Valdebebas to monitor the workload of his players and determine when they need additional recovery. Rather than applying identical restrictions across the squad, the coaching staff is assessing individual requirements. Minutes played, physical demands and the needs of upcoming fixtures will influence decisions about training intensity, selection and rest periods. This approach is particularly relevant for players who regularly feature across competitions. Guler and Tchouameni were rested against AEK Athens. item.title: Ponga-inspired New Zealand reach World Cup final
item.description: Kalyn Ponga featured with a protective arm guard for New Zealand [Getty Images] New Zealand (12) 34 Tries: Nikora, Gagai, McLean, Hughes, Willison, Nicoll-Klokstad Goals: Isaako 5 Tonga (10) 10 Tries: Fifita 2 Goals: Katoa Just 23 days after breaking his arm, Kalyn Ponga returned to inspire New Zealand to a 34-10 victory in a pulsating encounter with Tonga as they reached their first World Cup final since 2013. Ponga had been named initially in reserve and then as one of the interchange players in the build-up to this contest - and the expectation was that he would be eased back into action and play a limited role. Instead, head coach Stacey Jones stunned many with his decision to include Ponga in New Zealand's starting 13 but was repaid in full as the Newcastle Knights talisman starred on home turf at the McDonald Jones Stadium, in New South Wales, Ponga's impact from full-back was almost immediate as he sent Briton Nikora over in the right corner inside four minutes. He was also involved in the Kiwis' second try of the game - as his contest with his opposite number Lehi Hopoate was crucial to Dane Gagai grounding the ball. And while the swirling wind made conditions almost unplayable at times, he repeatedly gathered high kicks and made several telling defensive contributions. One of those included throwing himself in the way of Tonga's juggernaut second row Demitric Vaimauga to prevent a certain try, while his ability to stall Hopoate's run and prevent him from offloading to Isaiya Katoa stopped another at a key stage with New Zealand only 12-10 ahead. The prelude to this fixture was almost every bit as gripping as the main event. Tonga's traditional war dance, the Sipi Tau, was met by New Zealand's Haka and a long stand-off between the players provided the perfect backdrop to a contest brimming with athleticism, power and superb ball-handling skills. For the second week running, Tonga fans turned out in force with the stands a sea of red. And they witnessed their side's participation in a wonderful advert for rugby league with Jojo Fifita scoring two excellent tries. However, the match ultimately swung away from them in a five-minute period after the break when New Zealand's outstanding centre Casey McLean surged over in the left corner and the wily Jahrome Hughes darted in to score. On this occasion, Kristian Woolf's team, who effectively torpedoed England's hopes of reaching the last four with a 30-12 in their opening match on 17 October, were unable to stage the same sort of fightback that helped them defeat their Pacific Island rivals Samoa last weekend. With the scoreboard, time and a gale-force wind against Tonga, Xavier Willison punished them further when they failed to gather a short drop out. And when Charnze Nicoll-Klokstad superbly grounded Erin Clark's kick, it put the gloss on a fine New Zealand performance. item.title: Kimi Antonelli Won’t Rule Out Ferrari After Ecclestone Says ‘They Have to Do It’
item.description: Kimi Antonelli can’t see himself anywhere but Mercedes for now, but he isn’t ruling out Ferrari after Bernie Ecclestone predicted he’ll switch one day. Already, when he landed an F1 seat, the chatter grew that Antonelli would one day drive for Ferrari. A top Italian driver racing for the ultimate Italian team feels like a story written in the stars. For a long time, Ferrari has tried to get an Italian in its car. They got Giancarlo Fisichella back in the day and were preparing the likes of Antonio Giovinazzi and Antonio Fuoco for the ultimate switch, but it didn’t work out in the end. Both are still part of the Ferrari family in sports cars. But there is no doubt that Ferrari would keep an eye on Antonelli, even though they have the likes of Oliver Bearman and even Rafael Camara in their ranks as F1 juniors. Image Credit: James Sutton/LAT Images Ecclestone: ‘Kimi’s Heart Beats Italian’ For now, they are satisfied with Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc, but there is growing tension among them. With Antonelli now the F1 champion, his stock has gone up considerably, and the Italian pull is still there. Former F1 boss Bernie Ecclestone believes he will drive for Ferrari one day, for Italy. “Ferrari has no choice, they have to do it,” he told F1-Insider . “And Kimi’s heart beats Italian. If he continues to win, and I’m convinced he will, he’ll switch to Ferrari out of love for his country.” Even Piero Ferrari has kept the door open for Antonelli , even comparing him to Niki Lauda. His son reportedly wants an Italian in the team too. But does the newly crowned champion want it? He isn’t ruling it out. Antonelli Doesn’t Rule Out a Ferrari Move Image Credit: Clive Mason/Getty Images For now, it is all Mercedes for him, naturally. But in the future, who knows? “I wouldn’t see myself anywhere else but Mercedes, especially now,” said Antonelli in an interview with La Gazzetta dello Sport . “They signed me when I was 11, took a risk with me, and have always believed in me. “I’m incredibly happy with where I am, and I’m grateful for everything we’ve done together and will continue to do. They’ve become a second family to me, and I think I’ve really taken a big step this year when I realized the team accepted me for who I am. And then for the future, very far away, who knows. We’ll see,” he said.

item.title: Special teams loomed large in Sheridan football's playoff loss
item.description: COLUMBUS — A script-like night for football was "special" for Michael Thompson-Ayers and the rest of the East Tiger return men. Quite literally, it was their performance on special teams in their Division III, Region 11 quarterfinal matchup with visiting Sheridan that made this night memorable. Thompson-Ayers' 65-yard kickoff return for a touchdown was East's second long return of the half — Dominique Edwards had a 55-yarder on the opening kickoff — that impacted the game so much that visiting Sheridan didn't even kick their way until the final minute of the second half. It was the key factor in the third-seeded Tigers' 42-28 win before a festive crowd on Nov. 6 at Harley Field. East, a which lost in the Division IV quarterfinals in 2025, advanced to face unbeaten Licking Valley at 7 p.m. on Nov. 13 at Randy Baughman Stadium. Connors over the middle with 39 seconds left before halftime. With the Generals due to get the ball after halftime, it turned out to be a 14-point swing when Whiteman engineered a near-five-minute scoring drive to start the third quarter. Instead of a 14-13 lead, it was a 21-14 deficit five minutes into the second half. Sheridan coach Paul Culver III said in the case of both first-half returns, the plan was to squib kick the ball away from both deep men, preferably to the sideline to gain an extra defender. "Their kids got hands on them because we didn't get a solid kick on the ball," Culver lamented. "We thought the ball was going one way, maybe sliding out of bounds or into a corner, and it didn't. Our kids weren't angling that direction and that hurt us. "(Lou Goodlow and Thompson-Ayers) were their difference makers," Culver III added. "We looked slow and out of position at times, but that's my job to put our kids in position to be successful." The Generals spent the rest of the night playing catch-up against the Tigers' regiment of speedsters, and they did so defending half-fields due to the fear of the Tigers' return ability. They also dealt with 10 penalties measuring 105 yards, including multiple 15-yarders. Whiteman's second touchdown pass to Connors, on fourth-and-goal from the Tiger 14 after a Connor Roshon interception, got Sheridan within 28-21 with 8:01 left. But a 17-yard keeper from Dion Hansard was followed by a facemask and ensuing unsportsmanlike conduct penalty on Sheridan, that set up Edwards' 15-yard jaunt through traffic. item.title: Five takeaways from Norwich City's latest accounts
item.description: Although group turnover totalled £40.3m, the club recorded an operating loss before player trading - of £42.3m [Press Association] Norwich City Football Club has released its latest annual report, detailing the club's financial standing for the year until 30 June 2026. It shows the Canaries recorded an operating loss of £13.3m - despite making almost £46m in profit from selling players. Before taking player trading into account, the club recorded an operating loss of £42.3m , compared with a £25.5m loss in 2025.​ While the Championship side reported increases in areas including attendances, retail and sponsorship, its operating costs also rose sharply. Here are five key takeaways from the club's latest annual report. Rising operating costs Staff costs have increased at Norwich City [Press Association] According to the report, the club's operating costs rose to £99.8m, from £79.2m the previous year. Norwich City said this reflected its "continued investment in the playing squad and football operations". A large chunk of this figure is staff costs, which rose from £48.1m the previous year to £57.9m in 2026. These costs included wages, National Insurance, pensions and other employment costs. Within that figure, wages and salaries rose from £39.9m to £49.6m. Profit from selling players Norwich City striker Josh Sargent completed a move to Toronto FC in a deal worth more than £20m [Press Association] Norwich City did record significant profit from player sales. The departure of players such as Borja Sainz, Jonathan Rowe and Josh Sargent helped earn the club £45.9m profit from player trading, up from the £24.3m achieved in the previous year. The accounts also included £16.8m in player amortisation, an accounting process that spreads the transfer fees paid for players over the lengths of their contracts. After player trading was taken into account, the club's operating loss fell from £42.3m to £13.3m, which it said was "broadly consistent with the prior year's result". In the report the club said: "Player trading remains an important part of our financial model and generated profits of £45.9 million during the year, helping to offset underlying operating losses." Fan support remains strong Fan support has remained strong with a slight increase in shirt sales [Press Association] The average attendance at Norwich City's Carrow Road stadium was 25,899, while the club sold 20,039 season tickets. The club described this as "another strong year" for ticket sales. Retail revenue increased to £2.4m, helped by an 8.6% increase in replica shirt sales, with more than 29,000 shirts sold during the season. The report said figures showed "the incredible loyalty and commitment of our fanbase." Investment in the squad During this period the club has signed new players such as Mathias Kvistgaarden [Press Association] Norwich City has invested heavily in signing new players, with the accounting value of its player registrations rising from £32.6m to £53.9m. item.title: ‘Make sure you smile’: Rutgers coach Steve Pikiell continues to preach positivity amid cancer battle
item.description: Rutgers coach Steve Pikiell was on campus the day before his team’s season opener against New Haven, and he sent a message to acting head coach Brandin Knight hours before tipoff. “It’s funny, he said, ‘Make sure you smile,’” Knight recalled following the Scarlet Knights’ 81-54 victory at Jersey Mike’s Arena . “That was one of his big things, like have fun, enjoy it. It’s always about the guys but have a good time and smile. That’s the way he is. He can find some positivity in anything. Pikiell, 58, announced that he was battling cancer in September, and Knight, the 44-year-old who was brought on Pikiell’s staff in 2016 and had been his associate head coach the previous five seasons, was tabbed as acting head coach. While Pikiell focuses on his health, Knight draws inspiration from his boss, who contributes his time and thoughts where and when he can as he cycles through treatments and rests. “Coach is one of the strongest people I know,” Knight said. “He’s showing up here two or three times. He is showing how tough he is. It’s not easy to get out of bed and do things like that, but he comes around. He’ll sit and watch practice. He’ll give encouraging words.” Pikiell was not among the spectators at Jersey Mike’s Arena, but support for his fight was evident throughout the crowd with students and fans wearing red T-shirts emblazoned with “ Rutgers Tough ” across the chest. They were selling for $30, with 100 percent of proceeds going to RWJ Barnabas Health’s efforts in cancer treatment and patient care as part of a fundraiser envisioned by Pikiell. A video of former players like Caleb McConnell, Dylan Harper , Ace Bailey and Ron Harper Jr. talking about different examples of being “Rutgers Tough”played on the scoreboard above center court. Knight noted that the shirts sold out in the first day. Players will continue to wear them during warmups this season. The first $250,000 of the campaign is coming from Pikiell and his wife, Kate, “I hope it’s inspiring not only to myself and all of these guys,” Knight said. “Whatever you’re going through, whatever type of adversity you think you’re dealing with right now, it is nothing like the kind coach and his family has been dealing with.” Knight carried on the program’s signature approach to defense against New Haven, which is in its second season in Division I and the second year of a three-year transition from Division II. item.description: Photo by Al Pereira/Getty Images Shedeur Sanders has been named as the starting quarterback for the Cleveland Browns this weekend as they face the New Orleans Saints. Todd Monken confirmed on Friday that it would be Sanders taking the starting role for the Browns, with Deshaun Watson working his way through the concussion protocol following the recent loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. Sunday will mark the first start of the season for Sanders, who has been forced to watch from the sideline after Watson won the job over the offseason. However, the controversial young quarterback now has the opportunity to prove himself under Monken in a game situation. The 24-year-old completed both of his passes last weekend when he came into the game against the Steelers, and he has shown his confidence ahead of the game against the Saints. “The only way I see Shedeur Sanders starting for the rest of the season if they exceed any type of benchmark that was set like if I think it was like 300 yards plus,” said Newton on his YouTube channel. “If they have a 400-yard offensive day, oh man, we got to reconsider some stuff.” The chances of that happening against the Saints may not be as unlikely as Newton may think, though. The New Orleans Saints’ defense has allowed 372 yards of total offense per game on average this season. However, even with Watson at quarterback, the Saints have only managed to average 301 yards of total offense per game this season. So, sealing a 400-yard game with Sanders at quarterback would certainly be something. item.description: With the lockout looming at the end of the month, this offseason appears ready to heat up quickly, as teams are eager to get at least some of their business done before the baseball world freezes at the order of the league owners. While much of the attention has, so far, centered on the free agent market — options exercised and declined, qualifying offers extended, players from Japan and Korea posted — chances are, given Brian Cashman’s history, the Yankees will be just as active on the trade market, if not more so. Over the past decade, he has acquired Ryan Weathers, Cody Bellinger, Juan Soto, Trent Grisham, Josh Donaldson, Isiah Kiner-Falefa, Jameson Taillon, James Paxton, and Giancarlo Stanton in offseason deals. While it’s not yet clear who exactly will be available this winter, as the old saying goes, you have to give something to get something, so we can take a look at which players on the 40-man roster the Yankees might use to swing a deal. Major League starters They say you can never have enough pitching, and while that’s true, the Yankees are in the rare position where they have some depth to work with. Between presumptive AL Cy Young Cam Schlittler, 2023 AL Cy Young Gerrit Cole, and a pair of southpaws with multiple top-six finishes in Max Fried and Carlos Rodón, the Yankees starting rotation has quite an extensive resume. Obviously, no team wants to shed too much of its pitching depth — we said much the same thing about the Yankees’ 2025 rotation when they traded Nestor Cortes, only for them to need to turn Ryan Yarbrough into a starter and promote Schlittler mid-season — but still, this category represents the Yankees’ biggest trade chips, and for the right bat, it may very well be worth it…and it becomes a no-brainer if they sign Tarik Skubal as a replacement. Of the three, Will Warren seems to me to have the most value. Ironically, those very same reasons may also be why Weathers is the pitcher the team is more likely to lose. item.description: For the first time this season, Aaron Donald, left, and Myles Garrett will be playing together for the Rams on Sunday when they face the Washington Commanders. (Kyusung Gong, Doug Benc / Associated Press) It began as something merely conceptual, a tantalizing possibility. Last June, immediately after the Rams traded for star edge rusher Myles Garrett , the NFL grapevine began buzzing: Would Aaron Donald , a three-time NFL defensive player of the year, consider coming out of retirement to play with Garrett, a two-time winner of the award? After a summer of rampant speculation, Donald signed on to join what was already regarded as a Super Bowl-favorite team. But Donald’s ramp-up to achieve football shape precluded him from playing in the season opener against the San Francisco 49ers . And Garrett underwent knee surgery after that loss, so the two stars were unable to play together for seven games. On Sunday, it will finally happen. Barring an unexpected setback, Garrett and Donald will line up together for the first time when the Rams play the Washington Commanders at Northwest Field in Landover, Md. Two players accustomed to being double- or triple-teamed — two players with a combined 236½ sacks — are eager for opportunities. “The offenses are really going to have to pick their poison,” said Garrett, who amassed an NFL season-record 23 sacks last season. “‘Who’s going to be freed-up this play?’ “I think either of us are pretty good at winning one-on-ones, so we’ll have some fun.” Said Donald, one of the most dominant interior linemen in NFL history: “It’s always good when you’ve got all the pieces to the puzzles out there.” The Rams (4-4) aim to build on their modest two-game winning streak and get over .500 for the first time this season. The defense will be without cornerback Jaylen Watson, who suffered a season-ending shoulder injury in last Sunday’s victory over the Chargers . Cornerback Trent McDuffie is questionable after suffering a back injury against the Chargers and not practicing this week. Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald tackles New York Giants running back Najee Harris for a loss during a Rams win on Sept. 21 at SoFi Stadium. (Allen J. Schaben / Los Angeles Times) But Garrett’s return should energize a team that still intends to play in Super Bowl LXI at SoFi Stadium. The Rams have only 12 sacks, which is tied for 26th among 32 teams. Edge rusher Byron Young has a team-best 4½ sacks. Donald is still looking for his first. The attention the Commanders and future opponents must pay to Garrett and Donald will open play-making opportunities for others, Young said. “I always call it art,” he said of Garrett’s and Donald’s ability to excel despite double teams. “Because it’s not easy when you’ve got four hands on you 90% of the time. And they still make it work. “So it’s going to be fun. I can’t wait.” Defensive lineman Braden Fiske said players are acclimating to Garrett’s skill set and play style. item.description: Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is one of the best players in the NBA, but he has a wholesome side as well. The Oklahoma City Thunder superstar is a hero to many fans after winning back-to-back MVP titles, but as with any player, there are NBA supporters who dislike him. However, it looks like some of them are switching sides now. NBA fans react to Shai Gilgeous-Alexander’s wholesome moment with kids during Thunder vs Grizzlies In the third quarter of the game between OKC Thunder and the Memphis Grizzlies, Gilgeous-Alexander got on the ball and just as he unleashed a shot, he was fouled. The Canadian ended up sitting on the floor facing the court, and instead of getting up on his own, he turned around and faced a few kids sitting courtside. Gilgeous-Alexander reached out to them with his hands and pulled himself up, thus giving those kids a memory they will never forget. That has impressed many NBA fans, even his ‘haters’, who are all praising what he did. One wrote: “That was cool even though I hate him.” Another tweeted: “Never thought I’d say this in my life, but W Shai!” “Kids have no idea how cool this moment is going to be for them when they look back at this in five years. Honestly, just pure class from SGA,” said another. Another NBA fan reacted by saying: “He’s actually so goated for this!” “Most wholesome superstar of all time. They can’t make me hate him,” said another. The fans are right: Gilgeous-Alexander made those kids’ day, and he seems to have earned a few more fans in the process. In the game, the Thunder star scored 28 points and recorded three rebounds and four assists, along with a block and a steal. He is continuing to perform brilliantly for OKC, and even though he seems to be behind Luka Doncic and Victor Wembanyama in the MVP race, he could climb up very quickly. Every November, some of the world’s finest tennis players arrive in the French capital, collect their complimentary tournament merchandise, perhaps enjoy a croissant or two, and then lose to somebody ranked about 70 places below them. You see, playing tennis for 11 months is quite enough, and this past Wednesday was a wonderful example. Alexander Zverev lost. Novak Djokovic lost. Daniil Medvedev lost. Alex de Minaur lost. Frances Tiafoe lost. At one point, the tournament seemed less interested in determining its champion than establishing how quickly it could get everybody through passport control. And the funniest part? This happens almost every year. Paris Masters: Where Stars Go When They’ve Had Enough Paris Has Been Sending Players on Holiday for Years The tournament has a distinguished history of encouraging early vacations. In 2023, Carlos Alcaraz lost his opening match to Roman Safiullin, while Medvedev disappeared against Grigor Dimitrov at the same stage. A year later, Medvedev, Taylor Fritz, Andrey Rublev and Casper Ruud all lost their opening matches. Four Top 10 players, gone before the tournament had properly begun. This year, however, might be particularly special. Zverev arrived as the newly crowned world No. 1, having won two Grand Slams this season. Lorenzo Musetti promptly defeated him 7-6 6-2. The German led 5-2 in the opening tiebreak before losing five straight points. He then surrendered the second set with relatively little resistance. Medvedev, meanwhile, lost 6-4 6-4 to Ignacio Buse, a 22-year-old Peruvian who had never previously beaten a Top 10 opponent. The Russian complained about the playing conditions afterward and at this stage, one suspects he would prefer the Paris Masters to be played somewhere entirely different. Perhaps Dubai or his living room. Then came De Minaur. The Australian needed one victory to move into an ATP Finals qualifying position. He created 13 break points against Tomas Martin Etcheverry, converted one and lost 7-6 6-3. Clearly, he didn’t want to go to Turin. And Djokovic? The seven-time Paris Masters champion won the opening set 6-2 against qualifier Rinky Hijikata before losing 2-6 6-3 6-3. That ended his Turin hopes. Tiafoe somehow managed to outdo everybody. The American served for his match against Quentin Halys, then held four match points in the deciding tiebreak, lost all four, and eventually lost the match 6-3 1-6 7-6. item.title: Patriots inducting Rob Gronkowski into team’s Hall of Fame
item.description: FOXBORO, MA - SEPTEMBER 10: Rob Gronkowski #87 of the New England Patriots celebrates after a touchdown against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Gillette Stadium on September 10, 2015 in Foxboro, Massachusetts. (Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) Maddie Meyer Legendary New England Patriots tight end Rob Gronkowski will be inducted into the team’s Hall of Fame Saturday. Gronkowski beat out fellow Patriots legends Adam Vinatieri and Logan Mankins in a fan vote to become the 38th inductee. Gronk spent 9 seasons in New England after being drafted in the second round of the 2010 NFL Draft. The Patriots won the AFC East in each of Gronk’s seasons and made the Super Bowl 5 times, hoisting three Lombardi’s. Gronkowski ranks first in Patriots history with 80 total touchdowns (79 receiving and one rushing), and his 7,861 receiving yards are second in team history. Gronk’s connection with QB Tom Brady was often unstoppable on the field during their time in New England. The two went to go on to play for the Buccaneers before Gronk retired in March of 2019. Gronk’s ceremony comes the same weekend Brady is expected to call the Patriots vs. Packers game at Gillette Sunday afternoon as a broadcaster for the first time. item.description: Hansi Flick talks Raphinha, Eric, Rodri, Bernal, De Jong, Julian Alvarez ahead of Atletico Madrid vs Barcelona Barcelona will be eager to strengthen their grip at the top of the La Liga standings when they take on Atletico Madrid tomorrow at the Riyadh Air Metropolitano. The Blaugrana are currently only two points clear of the Rojiblancos and a defeat could see them lose the top position heading into the international break – something that Hansi Flick & co. will be eager to avoid. Ahead of the trip to the Spanish capital, Flick spoke to the media in his pre-match press conference, providing an update on the injured players among other things. Flick confirms duo’s return Confirming that Barcelona defensive duo Eric Garcia and Andreas Christensen are available for the game, the manager said: “Eric could start and both will be in the squad for tomorrow. I think Eric can start, but we’ll see.” Flick then spoke about the injury suffered by Rodri in the win over Aston Villa and whether that could have been avoided by more careful management of minutes, saying: “You can always do things better, but in this case I spoke with the player and we managed his minutes. He’s an experienced player and we talked. “We agreed on these things. I can’t do more. When you see the results, you think you could have done things differently, but that’s in the past now.” As for Frenkie de Jong starting as the replacement for the Spanish international in the lineup, Flick said: “I haven’t decided if he’ll start. It’s good to think about it tonight. We know his quality, but we also know Bernal’s. He did very well in the last match and I’m really enjoying him.” De Jong is pushing to start in Rodri’s absence. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Discussing the qualities that De Jong and Marc Bernal bring to the table, the manager elaborated: “Frenkie can play in several positions, not just as a ‘6’. item.description: The joy never left. That's what Hirving Lozano says. Body language analysts may conclude otherwise, but even with the suspensions, the disagreements and ultimately him being frozen out at San Diego FC, Lozano says he still felt that wave of emotion when he did take the field. "I’ve always had joy playing soccer. It’s what I like to do most, what I’m most passionate about. Playing soccer is something marvelous for me. So, every time I’m on the field, every time I touch a ball, I’m happy," he told USA TODAY Sports this week. "Right now, I’m playing, touching the ball, getting on the field, that’s the best for me, the best thing possible." Lozano is enjoying two returns: The first, being on the field with the LA Galaxy and scoring in a 4-1 win over Austin FC. A win over Real Salt Lake on Nov. 7, and the Galaxy would lock up a playoff place, with Lozano now fit and ready to help the team in the postseason after a hamstring issue kept him out for all of October. CHUCKYYYYY He scores in his first game back from injury. 🇲🇽 pic.twitter.com/nqVvpfnJge — Major League Soccer (@MLS) October 31, 2026 The other return, weeks earlier, saw him playing professional soccer again after that hold out with SDFC. Signed by the 2025 MLS expansion club as its franchise player, meant to be the perfect star to connect with supporters of a team that wants to be relevant with fans both in Southern California and northern Baja California, Lozano put together a strong campaign in helping SDFC top the Western Conference and secure a place in the Concacaf Champions Cup in its first season of play. But all was not well. Lozano was suspended in October 2025, and didn't recover his starting spot in the playoffs - though he played in the club's final four postseason games as they fell to the Vancouver Whitecaps in the conference finals. Prior to the season, SDFC general manager Tyler Heaps stated flatly in January 2026 that Lozano would "not be part of the sporting plans moving forward." Rather than move elsewhere, Lozano spent the first half of the year training on his own before an Aug. 7 move ot the LA Galaxy . "I’m very happy. The reception at the Galaxy, to be honest, has been marvelous, giving me the chance to play again. I’m putting in a lot of effort to try to get to my best level," he said this week. "I know it’s been a bit complicated just not being able to play the whole season, not having a preseason, but I’m going step by step trying to get better every day and I’m really very happy to be here." The second return is being part of the push to get the Galaxy into the playoffs and contending for another MLS Cup. Lozano's mini-renaissance, getting back on the field for the Galaxy and earning a recall to the Mexico national team for the first time since fall of the year before, was cut short by a hamstring issue. item.title: "I am convinced that the team will give their best version tomorrow."
item.description: "I am convinced that the team will give their best version tomorrow." Girona will play tomorrow at Montilivi against Almeria, in a challenging match against a solid team in good form. "It’s a tough and complicated game, but I trust that we will give our best version," said coach Quique Álvarez, who emphasized the importance of winning: "The standings at the top are very tight, and we are coming off a loss. We have things to improve." The coach warned that Almeria is capable of causing trouble at any moment, both when they dominate and when they play on the counterattack. "They have gone nine games without losing and have players who can hurt you at any moment." Additionally, he pointed out that the upcoming series of matches, against mid-to-high table teams, will be a good measure to assess the team's situation. To face the challenge, Girona wants to increase their aggressiveness in pressing. "Except for the match in Córdoba, what has hurt us the most has been the two red cards, against Castellón and Real Sociedad B." Despite this, the coach expressed confidence that the team will respond well: "I am convinced that tomorrow we will give our best version." A special match and support for Jastin The match will also have a special component for the coach, who will reunite with a childhood friend on Almeria's bench. About García Pimienta, he explained that they share a philosophy of play based on taking the initiative and being protagonists, although experience has allowed him to adjust some aspects. The coach also wanted to send a message of encouragement to Jastin, who is going through a tough time after working very well. "He has been unlucky. We can only encourage him and help him so he can have continuity." A very special tribute In his press conference, the coach expressed Girona's support for the family, friends, and fans of Tenerife. He explained that the squad would have understood if the match had not been played and that he understands that those closest to the situation might decide not to participate. "Now we have to focus on the tribute, which will be very beautiful." Finally, he confirmed that Girona will only lose three players (Vanat, Asprilla i Holmes Junior) due to the international break, but he insisted that all attention is now focused on tomorrow's match against Almeria.

item.title: Derrick Henry trade rumors end as Ravens make decision before NFL deadline
item.description: The Baltimore Ravens won't trade Derrick Henry before Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, keeping their future Hall of Fame running back through a four-game losing streak and a quarterback room that lost its top two players to injuries. Baltimore never considered moving the five-time Pro Bowler and recently told Henry it has no plans to deal him, according to league sources. The New York Giants did ask about a Ravens running back, but it was Justice Hill. Sources: the Ravens are not expected to deal RB Derrick Henry before Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline. https://t.co/sLo88OZAvu — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 7, 2026 Trade talk grew after quarterback Lamar Jackson needed surgery on his right thumb and backup Tyler Huntley's turf toe ended his season . Henry's history with two current head coaches also drew attention to possible landing spots . John Harbaugh coached him the past two seasons in Baltimore before taking the Giants job, and Mike Vrabel coached him in Tennessee before landing with the New England Patriots. Moving the 32-year-old still would've left Baltimore with roughly $12 million in dead money. His contract runs through 2027, when he's due a non-guaranteed $11 million base salary, so the Ravens can revisit his future in the offseason. Henry made clear after Thursday's loss that he isn't pushing for an exit. "I have not mentioned me going anywhere else," Henry said. "I'm saying, 'Let's go back to work. Let's try to get better and turn this thing around .'" Henry gets Jacoby Brissett at quarterback Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett (7) takes the field before they play the Denver Broncos | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Baltimore made its deadline move Friday, when the Jacoby Brissett trade became official . The Ravens received the veteran quarterback and a 2027 fifth-round pick from the Arizona Cardinals for a 2027 fourth-rounder and a 2028 seventh-rounder. Brissett started Arizona's first eight games, throwing for 1,719 yards with 10 touchdowns and seven interceptions. He also spent the past two seasons in Arizona with Ravens quarterbacks coach Israel Woolfork, which should speed up his learning curve. Henry needs a passer that defenses have to respect. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano went 10-of-18 for 60 yards and two interceptions in Thursday's 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, so Jacksonville crowded the line and held Henry to 57 yards on 17 carries, even with him taking direct snaps in the Wildcat. He's now been held under 60 rushing yards in four straight games. "It wasn't good enough. We've got to be better," Henry said. "[It was the] same story ." item.title: Liverpool star breaks silence on potential new contract
item.description: Liverpool star breaks silence on potential new contract Trey Nyoni contract talks underline Liverpool’s growing faith in a rising midfield star Liverpool are moving towards a new agreement with Trey Nyoni, a development that feels significant without carrying any immediate pressure. As Liverpool Echo reported, discussions with the midfielder’s representatives have been ongoing for several months and there is increasing confidence that a deal will be reached. That matters because Nyoni’s place in the first-team picture has changed considerably. When Liverpool sanctioned Curtis Jones’ sale to Inter Milan in August, there was a conscious decision not to bring in a replacement. The judgement internally was that Nyoni was ready for a more senior role, and the early weeks of the season have strengthened that view. There was also a firm show of intent from the club in the market. A £30m bid from Nottingham Forest late in the window was turned away, and Liverpool have since watched the 19-year-old become an increasingly trusted option for Andoni Iraola. His full Premier League debut in the 1-0 defeat to Arsenal offered further encouragement, with Nyoni acquitting himself well before making way for Dominik Szoboszlai. Nyoni impact growing at Liverpool The numbers behind his progress are compelling. Nyoni has already surpassed last season’s Premier League appearance tally and now sits on 12 senior outings in all competitions, including his first Liverpool goal in the 3-2 Champions League defeat to Fenerbahce. Those are visible signs of development, but the underlying data is arguably even more persuasive. Photo: IMAGO He leads Liverpool’s squad for Opta-defined defensive contributions, averaging 13.3 per 90 minutes. He also tops Liverpool midfielders for line-breaking passes with 18.2, a useful marker of his ability to move the game forward. In Europe, where he has started three of four group matches, his 92 per cent pass completion under high-intensity pressure is the best recorded in the competition’s new format so far. Contract talks reflect changing role There is no contractual rush, with more than three years still left on his current terms after signing fresh papers in June 2025. This is more about recognition than necessity. Liverpool want Nyoni’s status to match his growing importance, and that is often how elite clubs protect value while rewarding progress. Nyoni’s own stance suggests calm on all sides. He told Liverpool Echo: “At the minute I am just leaving to my agents to sort out. My main focus right now is playing football, performing every time I go on the pitch. The off the pitch stuff, I leave it to them to do.” That response will reassure Liverpool. There is no noise, no public pressure, and no hint of distraction. Instead, there is a young midfielder focused on opportunity and a club acting early to secure a player they clearly believe can shape the next phase of this squad.
